text: These airplane wingtips are bent up. I'll straighten them flat!

speaker: fitz
text:
Stop. Those bends are on purpose.
A wing lifts because air pushes harder underneath than on top.
At the tip, that air sneaks around to the top and spins into a swirl.
That swirl creates what engineers call induced drag.

speaker: gauge
text: So the bent tip blocks the swirl?

speaker: fitz
text:
It weakens it, so there's less drag.
On long flights, that saves a few percent of the fuel.
